items.title: Jason Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2025
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I remember Joe Williams had the same story about when he did the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis recording...

ctx.x: Right? Yeah. Either coming home from a gig or, you know, if you look at those like really consequential Blue Note records, a lot of those were started, you know, they started recording at that time. And you know I met Fred — well I’ll just start off with a story. I met Freddie Hubbard back in the late ‘90s and he told me a lot of those records that they made, you know, were recorded in the morning and so there were times when they would play a gig and they’d play several sets and it’d end at 3, 4, 5 in the…

I wonder if that’s, you know, adrenaline kicks in. Coffee and whatever else sometimes resulted in terrific records. I remember Joe Williams had the same story about when he did the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis recording and no one had gone to bed yet.
